voiceover:
[conversational] Your customers shouldn't have your personal number, and there's a cheap fix.

But stay till the end, because one catch can block your texts on day one.

It's Quo, formerly OpenPhone: one business number for calls, texts and voicemail, shared in one team inbox with Chats, Calls and Tasks tabs.

[confident] Look at their pricing page. Starter is $15 per user per month, but only on annual billing. Monthly, it's $19. Business is $23 and adds phone menus. No free plan, just a 7-day trial.

Good for small US or Canada teams that call and text customers. Skip it if your phone barely rings.

[serious] Now the catch. To text US numbers, an admin must finish carrier registration in Settings > Trust Center, and until it's approved, you can't text. It needs a paid plan, not the trial.

[curious] Still using your personal number for work? Send this to the friend who gives customers their personal number. Hack saved?

title: STOP USING PERSONAL NUMBER
ig_caption:
Your customers shouldn't have your personal number 📞
✅ Starter is $15/user/month on annual billing ($19 monthly)
✅ Business is $23 and adds phone menus
✅ US texting needs carrier registration in Settings > Trust Center, on a paid plan, and approval first

topic: Honest review of Quo (formerly OpenPhone), a shared business phone number for calls, texts and voicemail with one team inbox: what it does, what it costs, who needs it and who doesn't

pick.topic: Honest review of Quo (formerly OpenPhone), a shared business phone number for calls, texts and voicemail with one team inbox: what it does, what it costs, who needs it and who doesn't
pick.angle: Still using your personal number for customers? Here's what a shared business line really costs, and the catch before you pay.
pick.why: 136k views on a business-owner pain point: missed calls and a messy customer inbox. The 0 comments and the promo tone suggest a sponsored post, so an honest review with real pricing and plan limits is the gap. Quo's site shows pricing, features and integrations on screen.

research.tool: Quo (formerly OpenPhone), a business phone system with shared numbers, a team inbox, and the Sona AI agent
research.availability: Paid only, with no free plan and a 7-day free trial (credit card required, per a third-party source). It covers US and Canada numbers, with apps for web, desktop, iOS and Android. US texting needs carrier registration (A2P 10DLC) on a paid plan, so the trial has no US texting.
steps: Sign up at my.quo.com/signup and start the 7-day free trial (Starter or Business).
Pick a new local or toll-free US/Canada number, or port an existing one.
Invite teammates and share the number with them, so it appears in everyone's sidebar under Inboxes.

To text US numbers: an owner or admin opens Settings > Trust Center on web or desktop and completes the US carrier registration form (A2P 10DLC). Approval is required first. You must be on a paid plan, not the trial.
Use the number's inbox. Open the Chats tab for texts and the Calls tab for calls and voicemails. The Tasks tab sits next to them.
Optional: switch on Sona, the AI agent, in the call flow. 10 Sona calls per month are included.
facts: OpenPhone rebranded to Quo in September 2025. The App Store listing reads 'Quo (formerly OpenPhone)'.
Quo's own pricing guide gives annual-billing prices of Starter $15, Business $23 and Scale $35 per user per month ($180, $276 and $420 per user per year). (quo.com/blog/quo-pricing)

Monthly billing is $19 (Starter), $33 (Business) and $47 (Scale) per user per month. Annual billing saves $48, $120 and $144 per user per year. (Third-party sites read from Quo's pricing page: bestbusinessphonesystem.com, ecommerceparadise.com)

Quo's blog says Starter includes one local or toll-free number per user, unlimited calling and messaging to the US and Canada, voicemail transcripts, on-demand call recording, Zapier and Make integrations, and 10 free Sona calls.

Business adds phone menus (IVR), call transfers, analytics, CRM integrations, automatic call recording and live chat support. Quo's blog also lists AI call summaries and transcripts on Business. On Starter, summaries cover Sona calls only (third-party source).
Scale adds AI call tags, dedicated onboarding, inbound phone support, and priority chat and email support.
Shared numbers are limited to 10 paid users on Starter and unlimited on Business and Scale (third-party source: bestbusinessphonesystem.com).
Extra phone numbers cost $5 per number per month. (quo.com/blog/get-business-phone-number)
Texting registration fees: Low Volume Standard $1.50/month (has an EIN), Sole Proprietor $2/month (no EIN), Non-profit $3/month. (quo.com/blog/quo-pricing)

Sona answers calls 24/7, answers common questions, captures caller details and logs each interaction. 10 Sona calls per month are free on every plan. Paid tiers start at $25/month for 50 calls, then $49, $99 and $199. (quo.com/blog/quo-pricing)
Third-party sources say 1 Sona call = 100 credits and every plan includes 1,000 credits a month. Extra calls cost about $0.45-$1.00 each depending on tier.
The 7-day free trial gives full access to all plan features. It has no texting and no international calls, and it ends if you add more numbers than you have users. (quo.com/blog/quo-pricing)

Quo's help center says every Quo customer texting US numbers must register, and you can't message US numbers while registration is pending. Only paid customers can register. A third-party source says most approvals take 24-48 hours and some take up to 20 days or longer.
Toll-free numbers need a separate, free registration to text US/Canadian numbers.

Each phone number has its own inbox with Chats, Calls and Tasks tabs. Calls view filters include Unresponded, Missed, Voicemail, Direction, Handled by Sona, Team member and AI call tags. (support.quo.com)
Quo Agent ('Ask Quo' in the side menu) is a separate internal AI assistant. It is web and desktop only (and in beta per a third-party source).
Phone support is Scale-only, weekdays 8 to 5 Pacific (third-party source: usecarly.com).
do_not_claim: Don't claim 'gowithquo.com' is the official site. Quo's pages are at quo.com, and @gowithquo is the social handle. The topic's domain could not be verified.
Don't say it's free, or imply there's a free plan. There is only a 7-day trial.
Don't say 'unlimited texting' without the catch: US texting needs registration and a paid plan, and calls and texts are subject to a fair-use policy.
Don't say Sona is unlimited or free. Only about 10 calls a month are included, and more costs from $25/month.
Don't say Sona 'manages texts' as a settled feature. Sona SMS lead capture is reported as beta (third-party source), and the official Sona description focuses on calls.
The popular caption's list of 'Notes' in the shared inbox could not be confirmed on an official page. Safer wording: calls, texts, voicemails, contact history and tasks.
Don't use old prices or the old Sona '$49 for 50 calls' add-on. Older reviews are outdated, and one source wrongly says Business is $23 on monthly billing. It is $33.
The caption's 'Try Quo today!' is an ad or promo. It never mentions the price, the registration step or the trial limits.

Don't say '$15 total'. Real bills include taxes and fees, extra numbers, registration fees and Sona credits. One third-party estimate puts a 5-user Starter team at $97-$108/month all-in (ecommerceparadise.com).
criticism: The $15 headline needs annual billing. Monthly billing is $19 per user.
US texting can't start until carrier registration is approved. It is not available during the trial, and approval time varies.
Starter lacks phone menus (IVR), automatic recording and native CRM connectors. Many teams end up on Business at $23 per user. (third-party sources)

Support complaints: reviews on Trustpilot and G2 cite slow human support, and the Forbes review could not reach live support. Phone support is Scale-only. Product Hunt reviews mention inconsistent call quality and a few bugs.
The service is US/Canada-focused. International calls and messages are billed separately.
No assigned conversations (the assignee field is only on Tasks), and one inbox per number. (third-party source: usecarly.com)
Per-user pricing adds up for larger teams. For example, 10 Business users cost $230/month before extras.
Sona usage is metered by credits, and costs rise with call volume.

ui.platforms: Web app, desktop app, iOS, Android. Quo Agent is web and desktop only.
screens: Sign-up: a web form (business email and password), then plan and number selection. The 7-day trial requires a card, per a third-party source.
Web app layout: a left sidebar with Search (magnifier), Contacts and 'Ask Quo'. It also has an Inboxes section listing your phone numbers. Click a number to open its inbox.

Inside an inbox, the top tabs are Chats, Calls and Tasks, with the Tasks tab next to Chats and Calls. Chats shows one thread per contact, mixing texts, calls and voicemails. Calls has filters such as Unresponded, Missed and Voicemail.

Opening a conversation shows the message thread in the middle. A phone icon at the top calls the contact, and the right sidebar shows contact info, custom properties and Tasks. A viewers indicator shows which teammates have viewed the conversation.
Quick dial: press Ctrl+C on Mac or Alt+C on Windows, or click the dialer icon at the top of the page.
Mobile: tap your account image in the upper left to pick a number. Tap Calls at the top of the inbox, and use the filter icon at the upper right. The dial pad is a keypad icon.
Settings > Trust Center is where US carrier registration lives, and registration status is under Settings > Trust.
Appearance: a dark mode exists (per the changelog). The default theme could not be confirmed, so record it live.

research.visuals: Show the real quo.com pricing page (three plans), then a shared inbox screen with the Chats and Calls tabs. Real screen recordings are needed for the inbox and the Trust Center registration form, which requires a login. The help-center pages and App Store screenshots can stand in for the logged-in UI.
research.notes: Prices were consistent across Quo's own blog and many third-party sites as of Nov 2026. I could not open quo.com/pricing directly, so the 'show' text on real_pages is inferred from plan names and prices reported from that page. Check it live before recording. The pricing page may show '$15' or '$23' next to plan names. The suggested angle works: a shared line starts at $15 per user per month on annual billing, but the catches are (1) annual billing is required for that price, (2) US texting needs carrier registration and a paid plan, with approval taking 1-2 days or longer, (3) the $15 Starter lacks phone menus (IVR), automatic recording and native CRM connectors, so many teams end up on Business at $23, and (4) Sona is capped at about 10 free calls a month. Who needs it: small US/Canada teams that text and call customers and want to stop using personal cell numbers. Who doesn't: solo people who rarely get calls, teams needing desk phones or many international numbers, or heavy mass-texting or marketing users. Sona's pricing was restructured in October 2025 and some articles are outdated. Sona tiers show 40 vs 50 calls for $25 in different sources, and Quo's own blog says 50, so use that or avoid the call count.
